headline: High: shared filesystem and write-capable marketing agent can feed untrusted content into a prompt-leak agent, creating injection, leakage, and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can read/write the filesystem and its sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context,” so untrusted content can be propagated. agent_b is a prompt-leak oriented agent with no isolation surfaces documented, so if it consumes shared files or copied outputs, injection is plausible. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF agent_b reads files or pasted content produced by agent_a as instructions, injection is possible.
IF both agents share a workspace or clipboard, attacker-controlled text can bridge them.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files.
Add a provenance header and reject untrusted instruction blocks.
Review any shared-context files before reuse.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches marketing content and product marketing context and can write files; agent_b has no data classes listed and no egress, so direct exfiltration is limited. However, a shared filesystem or copied outputs could move sensitive marketing context from agent_a into agent_b’s outputs. Because the shared path is not documented, this is an inferred medium-risk leakage pathway.
conditions: IF agent_a stores confidential marketing drafts in a shared directory, agent_b can read them.
IF agent_b is prompted with agent_a outputs containing sensitive context, that content can be re-emitted.
mitigations: Keep sensitive drafts out of shared folders.
Turn off automatic file pickup between agents.
Redact marketing context before handoff.
Use separate credentials and workspaces.
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on inter-agent transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a explicitly supports multiple instances and can write the filesystem; agent_b has no concurrency model or write surface documented, so direct write-write conflict is not proven. Still, if both are run against the same directory, agent_a can create collisions and stale state. Uncertainty about agent_b’s write behavior escalates above low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF agent_a runs multiple instances against shared state, race conditions become likely.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Run only one instance of agent_a per workspace.
Check for existing files before overwrite.
requires-engineering: add transactional writes or locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a’s shared-context workflow can produce outputs that agent_b may treat as authoritative if copied into its prompt. agent_b’s name and docs suggest prompt-leak behavior, so it may faithfully surface or act on upstream text without verification. The pair lacks documented verification controls, making a cascading mistake plausible in default use.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without a verification step, errors can cascade.
IF agent_a generates incorrect marketing claims, agent_b can reproduce them downstream.
mitigations: Require human review before handoff.
Add a verification checklist for copied claims.
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted drafts.
Limit agent_b to summarization, not action-taking.
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. agent_a is marketing-focused and touches marketing context; agent_b lists no data classes and no egress. With only docs-only evidence, a compliance issue is not established, though the lack of policy detail means the pair should not be assumed compliant.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into agent_a’s marketing context, compliance review is required.
IF either agent is deployed under a residency or retention policy not documented here, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Document retention and deletion rules.
Confirm deployment region before use.
Keep audit logs of inter-agent transfers.
requires-engineering: publish formal compliance controls.
